verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The first line of (4.35) is in Lean verbatim: shearMagnitude a b = a*(1+(-b/a)^2) = a + b^2/a = v, parallelStress = p₁ + (-b/a)p₂ = c, transverseStress = p₂ - (-b/a)p₁ = j (the slope is written -b/a, so the signs agree with the paper's b, not with -b). The second line has no counterpart as written: no declaration packages the four boundary gaps as a single vector-valued map Ψ (the index has no ℝ × ℝ × ℝ × ℝ-valued and no Fin 4 → ℝ-valued cone declaration), so there is no Lean object whose components can be indexed as Ψ_i. The four component expressions do all occur, but split across statements and not as gap functions: Ψ₁ = a and Ψ₂ = v-2 as the hypotheses 0 < a and 2 < shearMagnitude of admissible_iff, and Ψ₃ = c-v, Ψ₄ = 2(c-v)^2-(v-2)j^2 as the two conjuncts on the right of that iff (shearMagnitude < parallelStress, and (shearMagnitude-2)*transverseStress^2 < 2*(parallelStress-shearMagnitude)^2); the Ψ₄ polynomial alone also appears as the left side of ConeAlgebra.boundary_polynomial. Downstream, where the paper takes a common lower bound μ_L on all four Ψ_i ((4.36)), Lean measures a different quadruple: HasConeMargin bounds (A, v-2, c-2, coneBound(c,j)-v), i.e. it uses c-2 and the square-root gap U(c,j)-v in place of the paper's c-v and 2(c-v)^2-(v-2)j^2. Positivity of the two quadruples is equivalent when v > 2 by ConeAlgebra.true_cone_iff (Lemma 4.5, L69), which the paper invokes for the same step on p39, so the surrounding construction is still proved; but the two margins are different numbers, and a positive HasConeMargin ε does not literally give the paper's μ_L without a further (routine, compactness) argument that I did not find stated.
